hypotheses.title: SemTypeInterner scans each (all,some) bucket linearly, making opaque lang-lib call monomorphization O(N^2) per function body
hypotheses.issue: semtypes.SemTypeInterner.Intern/Lookup bucket complex semtypes only by their (all, some) basic-type bitsets and then walk the bucket's dataLists linearly with sameSubtypeDataList (identity comparison; int/float/decimal/string subtype data never compares equal). Every list type lands in one bucket and every mapping type in another, so each intern/lookup costs O(#types already interned with the same bitsets). The hot user is the opaque lang-lib monomorphization cache in stage 5 (Local Type Resolution): resolveOpaqueCallArgs -> opaque FunctionDefinition.Monomorphize -> ctx.lookupMono/storeMono -> monoCacheNodeFor/monoCacheChild -> monoInterner.Intern(key). Each `int[]`/`map<int>` type descriptor yields a distinct semtype (fresh definition atom), so every opaque call (push, get, indexOf, remove, ...) on a new local misses and appends to the bucket, and every later intern rescans it: O(N^2) for a function body with N such calls. Each miss also materializes a fresh monomorphic FunctionSymbol for a structurally identical type (secondary duplicate work, not addressed by the prototype). The same interner also backs semtypes.Context memos, SemTypeCache and TypePool, so the linear scan is a general hazard.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproducer: one function body with many locals of (structurally identical) collection type,
each receiving a lang-lib opaque call (array:push / map:get).

Every `int[]` / `map<int>` type descriptor yields a distinct semtype (fresh definition atom), so each
call is a miss in the per-resolver monomorphization cache (semantics/internal/opaque/context.go).
Each lookup/store interns the key with semtypes.SemTypeInterner.Intern, which linearly scans every
previously interned type that shares the same (all, some) basic-type bitset -> O(N^2).

usage: gen_opaque_interner.py N [arrays|mixed] > repro.bal   (N = number of collection locals)
"""
import sys

n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 16000
mode = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "arrays"
out = ["public function main() {", "    int total = 0;"]
for i in range(n):
    if mode == "arrays" or i % 2 == 0:
        out.append(f"    int[] a{i} = [{i}];")
        out.append(f"    a{i}.push({i});")
    else:
        out.append(f"    map<int> m{i} = {{k: {i}}};")
        out.append(f"    total += m{i}.get(\"k\");")
out.append("    if total < 0 { panic(error(\"unreachable\")); }")
out.append("}")
print("\n".join(out))
reproducer.command: python3 gen_opaque_interner.py 16000 arrays > repro_opaque.bal; go build -o bal ./cli/cmd; hyperfine --warmup 1 --runs 5 './bal run repro_opaque.bal'; ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> repro_opaque.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: Within each (all, some) bucket, keep a hash index: a map from a fingerprint of the subtype-data list to the latest index with that fingerprint, plus a parallel next-chain slice; collisions are resolved with the existing sameSubtypeDataList. The fingerprint mixes the list length with maphash.Comparable of each element, but only for an allowlist of known comparable concrete types (*bddNodeImpl, *bddNodeSimple, bddAllOrNothing, *xmlSubtype, booleanSubtype, nil); unknown types hash only reflect.TypeOf to avoid panics on non-comparable values. Lists containing int/float/decimal/string subtype data can never match, so they are appended without scanning or indexing, and Lookup returns a miss immediately. The handle scheme (base/index) and reset() are unchanged. Pitfalls: properSubtypeData values must not be hashed generically (non-comparable dynamic types would panic); the per-bucket index costs a little memory. A follow-up could key the mono cache on a structural/canonical form of the receiver type to avoid materializing a fresh mono FunctionSymbol per structurally identical type.
